LESSON: INTERNATIONAL TRADE

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: BUSINESS STUDIES
Strand: Government and Global Influence in Business
Topic 3.2: International Trade
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 18

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers International Trade, part of Government and Global Influence in Business in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 BUSINESS STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: How does an economy benefit from international trade?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on International Trade together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Digital literacy: learner enhances skills of connecting and interacting with digital technology when using digital

devices with assistive technology to search for information on the appropriate digital applications or platforms

used in international trade.

● Self-efficacy: learner develops effective communication skills when debating on the advantages and disadvantages

of international trade.

● Critical thinking and problem solving: learner develops interpretation and inference skills when carrying out a

survey in the community on local products that can be developed for export.

Values:
● Love: learner respects others opinions when brainstorming and presenting on the meaning, classification and

importance of international trade, balance of trade and balance of payment.

● Respect: learner shows regard for the input of every member of the team when debating on the advantages and

disadvantages of international trade.

● Peace: learner works in harmony when brainstorming and presenting on the meaning and importance of

international trade.

● Social justice: learners exercise equity as they accord privileges without favour when using digital devices with

assistive technology or print or braille media to search for information as well as when carrying out a survey in the

community.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

● Peer Education and Mentorship: learner enhances interpersonal relationships when debating on the advantages and

disadvantages of international trade.

● Financial Literacy: Learner financial skills is enhanced when searching for information on the documents used in

international trade.

● Social cohesion: learners' unity is enhanced when learners participate in carrying out a simple survey in the

community on local products that can be developed for export.

40

● Internet Safety and Security: responsible online behaviour is enhanced as a learner uses digital devices with

assistive technology to search for information on the appropriate digital applications or platforms used in

international trade.

Suggested Learning Resources

● Business Studies curriculum design

● Business Studies handbook

● Digital device with assistive technology

● Approved textbooks and reference materials

● Photographs and pictures, embossed pictures.

● Charts, tactile charts

● Case study extracts

● Survey tools

● Research tools

Suggested Key Skill(s)

● Assessing concept of taxation in Kenya.

● Analysing types of custom duties in Kenya.

● Evaluating trends in taxation in Kenya.

● Exploring digital applications in International trade.

● Mapping local products that can be developed for export.
